correctness.rationale: For all integer \(M\ge4\) and \(n\ge1\), the published symbolic coding identifies nontrivial primitive words with physical primitive orbits. The proof independently derives the signed monomial Jacobian, decomposes it into \(d=\gcd(M,k)\) permutation cycles, proves that each cycle exponent includes \(k/d\) right-step factors, and obtains a sharp bound using the smallest prime divisor. A primitive p-right word with consecutive right symbols attains the bound whenever \(n>p\). The converse forces exactly p rights and an empty cyclic left gap. The circular independent-set count removes all other p-right words; because p is prime, adjacent-right extremizers cannot be proper powers. Cases \(n\le p\) and \(n=1\) are handled separately. The dependency-free checker passed 110 exhaustive small dimension-period comparisons and constructed 1,440 physical periodic points in exact rational arithmetic. Finite checks are supporting, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source identifies nonuniform expansion without a least-period rate; a sharp period-by-period minimum is a naturally motivated refinement of a dynamical stability invariant. The exact prime-divisor cutoff distinguishes prime from composite ambient dimension, determines the smallest multiplier achievable at every least period, classifies all minimizing itineraries, and enumerates all their cycles. The even-dimensional uniqueness phenomenon and general polynomial multiplicities are structural dynamical consequences, not arbitrary numerical facts or cosmetic restatements of the known \(M=3\) case.
